subject: Joint spatial model (joint linear predictor with covariates)

messages.author: 38116b1dfc834c58
messages.subject: Joint spatial model (joint linear predictor with covariates)
parts:
Hi,

I would like to fit a joint spatial model with the following structure in the linear predictors:

linear predictor Model 1:
eta1(s) = alpha1 + beta1*Cov1(s) + GP1(s)

linear predictor Model 2:
eta2(s) = lambda*eta1(s) + alpha2 + beta2*Cov2(s) + GP2(s)

legend:
linear predictors: eta1, eta2
intercepts: alpha1, alpha2
covariates: Cov1, Cov2
coefficients: beta1, beta2
Gaussian processes: GP1, GP2

Both Model 1 and Model 2 have a Bernoulli likelihood and the responses are observed at the same locations between the models. The linear predictor of Model 2 includes the linear predictor of Model 1 multiplied by a coefficient lambda.
I am not sure how to use the "copy" feature in R-INLA for an entire linear predictor, especially when covariates are present in the linear predictors.
Could anyone provide a guidance on how to:
a) write the INLA formula that will be in the command "inla":, i.e form<- Y ~ 0+...
b) write the stack data for model 1, 2 and both, i.e. stack1 <-inla.stack(...) ; stack2 <-inla.stack(...) ; stack12 <-inla.stack(...)

Many thanks!
Cheers
 
Andre
